steps.u: Prices on the product page are sometimes stale right after our nightly bulk price update. Find out why and fix it.

steps.a: I'll look at how the price cache is filled and when it is invalidated.

steps.r:
export async function getPrice(id){ const hit=await redis.get('price:'+id); if(hit) return hit; const p=await db.price(id); await redis.set('price:'+id,p,'EX',3600); return p }
export async function invalidate(ids){ await redis.del(ids.map(i=>'price:'+i)) }
await db.tx(async t=>{ for (const u of updates) await t.setPrice(u.id,u.price) }); await invalidate(updates.map(u=>u.id))

steps.a: Found it: invalidate runs right after the transaction, but a reader that missed the cache just before the commit can refill the key with the old price after the delete. That is a classic race between invalidation and refill.

  const hit=await redis.get('price:'+id+':'+ver);

i.old_string: export async function invalidate(ids){ await redis.del(ids.map(i=>'price:'+i)) }

steps.a: Fixed: entries are now keyed by a version counter that invalidation increments, so a late refill writes under the old version and is never read.

reference.summary: Fixed stale prices after bulk updates, caused by a race where a reader refilled the cache with the old price after invalidation; cache entries are now versioned so invalidation bumps a counter instead of deleting keys.
facts: stale prices after a nightly bulk update
race between cache invalidation and refill
cache keys now carry a version that invalidation increments
pricing tests pass at the end

specific: race condition between invalidation and refill

decisions.choice: version the cache key instead of deleting it on invalidation
decisions.reason: a late refill with the old value can no longer overwrite fresh data because it lands under the old version
